dishes.pairing_mechanics: Because norin is served cold, the pairing is not a temperature contrast but a salt-and-fat balance: light, clean water softens the saltiness of qazi and pepper and keeps the palate fresh; glass bottle fits festive tables
dishes.physiological_impact: Horse fat and qazi are rich and salty; black pepper builds thirst; commonly eaten at weddings and morning gatherings in Tashkent
dishes.fat_and_spice_profile: Very thinly cut boiled dough noodles mixed with finely sliced boiled horse meat and horse sausage (qazi), onion and black pepper; served cold or room temperature, sometimes with hot broth on the side

framework.name: COCA_COLA_EMOTIONAL

do: Use family words: oila, dasturxon, mehmon, ona, buvi
End with a shared toast of water
voiceover.music: Soft dutar / rubab motif or piano; no drops
voiceover.voice: Mature, calm male or female voice; conversational, like a relative speaking at the table

ru: Самые тёплые моменты - с самой чистой водой.
uz: Eng qadrli lahzalar - eng toza suv bilan.

framework.visual_style: Golden-hour or warm tungsten light (2700-3200K), soft diffusion, slow dolly-ins and gentle handheld, 24fps, shallow depth of field on hands and faces, long takes (3-5s), steam and candle/fire glow, product appears late (after second 6) and is poured for someone else, never for oneself
framework.neural_target: Hippocampus & Prefrontal Cortex (episodic memory, social-reward valuation)
framework.narrative_tone: Warm, slow, respectful, multi-generational; the product is a supporting character, family is the hero
framework.primary_trigger: Nostalgia, tradition and belonging. BioLife is positioned as the quiet, constant presence at the family dastarkhan - the water that is always on the table when the people you love are together.
framework.selection_rationale: Weddings are about family honour and tradition; being 'the water on every wedding table' anchors the brand in the most important life events.

guardrails.note: Never show alcohol; position BioLife as the table water of choice for halal celebrations.

month_context: Teachers' Day (Oct 1), peak wedding season, grape and cotton harvest

primary_event.emotional_state: Festive joy, family honour, generosity, pride; also fatigue for hosts
cultural_rituals: Nahor oshi (morning wedding osh for men)
Evening banquet with norin, salads and shashlik
semiotic_symbols: Bride in white with atlas details
Glass bottles in rows on tables
primary_event.physiological_state: Multiple heavy feasts per week (nahor oshi at dawn, evening banquets for 300-1000 guests); little sleep, long hours of dancing, high salt and fat intake
